synopsis: The system automatically brakes when an operator fails to react to a proximity warning, but ISO 21815 treats collision systems as assistance and retains operator responsibility because the technology cannot cover every situation [f1, f5836, f3647]. Validation therefore requires assumptions about operator behavior and timing, yet the booklet found neither a field-measured distribution of warning-response times nor a validated off-road operator model; it recommends sensitivity testing with uncertain operator response [f11484, f11481, f11829, f11485]. Automatic stops introduce restraint and cab-safety concerns: seven of 12 drivers killed in US haul-truck dump-point cases during 2005–2021 were unbelted, and MSHA engineers estimate that adequate seat belts, provided and worn, could save three to four miners annually [f3628, f3001, f3625]. Workers reported jarring and concerns about forceful stops, while MSHA stated in 2017 that it knew of no resulting on-board operator injuries; this remains unresolved and unmeasured, supporting caution rather than a quantified injury claim [f3392, f3394, f3619]. The booklet recommends jerk-limited deceleration and operator action before braking release, while site acceptance expectations include operator review of false and correct interventions plus training and competence evidence [f13638, f6158, f11137, f11145].
